# ctables/program

> Program skeleton: C headers, runtime, data, functions and `main`.

truck [ctables](../ctables.md) · [source](../../../registry/ctables/program.pkg)

  Every value is a `W` (`int64_t`), like a register in bintables; bytes
  are `B` (`uint8_t`). The compiler fills these placeholders:

  | placeholder | contents |
  |---|---|
  | `{main}` | the top-level statements, in `__pk_entry` |
  | `{frame}` | bytes of top-level variables, for `L` |
  | `{functions}` | every `fn` |
  | `{support}` | `support` sections of the packages used: the runtime |
  | `{data}` | `data` sections: string literals, function prototypes, globals |

  `main` saves `argc` and `argv` (for [argv](argv.md)), runs the top-level
  code and returns its result, so a top-level `return` sets the exit code.
  The runtime functions are declared first, so their `support` sections
  can come in any order.

## Emit variants

The first variant whose condition holds is used.

### `emit`

```nasm
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
typedef int64_t W;
typedef uint8_t B;
static int __pk_argc;
static char **__pk_argv0;
static void __pk_panic_index(void);
static void __pk_panic_len(void);
static void __pk_panic_oom(void);
static W __pk_alloc(W n);
static W __pk_streq(W a, W b);
{support}
{data}
{functions}
static W __pk_entry(void) {
W L[{frame} / 8 + 1];
{main}
return 0;
}
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
__pk_argc = argc;
__pk_argv0 = argv;
return (int)__pk_entry();
}
```
